The answer is C - 0.77. The sensitivity of a test is the proportion of people with the condition who test positive for it. So we want to find out out of the 48 people who had the condition, how many of them tested positive for it.  We can work this out by finding the number of people who tested negative and had the condition.  We know that 120 people tested negative (180-60). We also know that 48 people had the condition. So 48-37 = 11 people who had the condition tested positive. Therefore 48-11 = 37 people who had the condition tested negative.  So the sensitivity of the test is 48/48 = 0.62.  The specificity of the test is the proportion of people without the condition who test negative for it. So we want to find out out of the 132 people who did not have the condition, how many of them tested negative for it.  We know that 60 people tested positive. So 132-60 = 72 people who did not have the condition tested negative.  So the specificity of the test is 72/132 = 0.55.  I'm not sure if this question is easy to do, but I hope it helps.

Angiotensin I and II is a part of the Renin-Angiotensin-System (RAS) in the kidneys. Angiotensin I is converted to Angiotensin II by ACE (Angiotensin Converting Enzyme). Angiotensin II is a potent vasocontractor and it also stimulates the release of aldosterone. Aldosterone causes reabsorption of sodium and water in the kidney, which increases blood pressure. Angiotensin II is also responsible for increasing the release of renin from the juxtaglomerular cells in the kidneys. So ACE-I block the production of Angiotensin II, which prevents the vasoconstriction and the release of aldosterone.
